about: The tool-round budget of one turn, the same in both SDKs (2026-09-28): the default and the bounds, the round at which the model is told to stop calling tools (half way through a budget of 20 or less, 80% of a larger one), the words the model gets, the reasons a turn ends with, and what the chat asks. A turn that reaches its budget, or makes the same tool call `repeat_limit` times IN A ROW with the same result each time, makes ONE more model call with tools off and a wrap-up message, so it always ends with an answer when the model gives one. A repeat counts only when nothing changed in between (2026-09-29): any other call between two repeats, or a different result, starts the count over, so an edit-and-rerun cycle is not a loop (`repeats`: `calls` are [tool, arguments, result] in order, `looped_at` the 1-based call at which the detector first answers, null when it never does; `edit_and_rerun`: a stub model that runs a script, rewrites it, runs it again, twice, then answers). `scenario` is a stub model that asks for a tool whenever it has tools, run under a budget of `limit`; `loop` one that repeats a call. Python: webagents/agents/core/tool_budget.py, tests/test_tool_round_budget.py; TypeScript: src/core/tool-budget.ts, tests/unit/core/tool-round-budget.test.ts.

repeats.name: the same call with the same result three times in a row is a loop
an edit between two runs starts the count over, even when the run fails the same way
the same command with a different result each time is not a loop
the order of the arguments does not matter
a streak broken by another call starts over from the next repeat

loop.says: The agent stopped early: it called list_directory 3 times in a row with the same arguments and got the same result each time.

one_detector.note: ONE repeated-call detector per SDK (2026-09-29): `RepeatedCalls`, recorded after each result. The TypeScript agent had kept an older one beside it, keyed per whole round on the arguments alone (with `delegate` messages and `text_editor` paths normalised), which rewrote the third identical round's tool result into a nudge (the second's for `delegate`); it is gone, and the Python agent never had one. On a true loop the model has `results_seen` unchanged tool results in front of it on the last call, each as the tool returned it, and the client's tool_result events carry the same; the wrap-up system message (`loop_answer`) is the only thing added. `old_nudge` is a phrase of the removed rewrite; it never appears in what the model or the client gets.
